text:
Ten years after he scored his first NHL goal on Philipp Grubauer, Sebastian Aho scored twice more on him, this time in Helsinki, in front of a Finnish crowd, in the first game of the NHL Global Series Finland. NHL.com's Tom Gulitti noted the anniversary; the rest of the afternoon was the Hurricanes making sure the homecoming had no drama in it. Carolina beat Seattle 4-1 for its third straight win, on a night that also belonged to Taylor Hall, who played his 1,000th NHL game with every Hurricane wearing his 71 in warmups.

The first period settled it early. Nikolaj Ehlers opened the scoring at 11:44 on a wrist shot our model gave a 3% chance of going in, the least likely goal of the game, and 66 seconds later Aho tipped in a power-play goal to make it 2-0. Carolina had 1.09 expected goals (the quality of chances) to Seattle's 0.46 in that period. Juuso Välimäki added a snap shot in the second, and by then our win probability had the Canes at 93%. Aho's slapper in the third made it 4-0 before Frederick Gaudreau broke Brandon Bussi's shutout bid at 13:15.

The shot totals tell you what kind of game it was: 30 to 13 on goal, 84 to 37 in attempts. Seattle blocked 20 shots and threw 23 hits, which is what a team does when it spends most of the night without the puck. The Kraken's one real look came in the second, when Ben Meyers got a 26% chance and Bussi stopped it, the biggest save of the game. Bussi faced only 13 shots but still saved a goal more than they deserved and added the most wins of anyone on the ice.

Carolina deserved this one about 71% of the time by our replays of every shot, and it has the feel of a team that travels well. For Seattle, a few days after trading Shane Wright for Matthew Wood, it was a long afternoon of chasing a team that rarely gave the puck back.
headline: Aho comes home and beats Grubauer again
